summary: Wooden tower with a Gothic Revival keeper's house, first lit April 1, 1886 at Jamestown, RI. Deactivated 1933; now a closed private residence.

structures.type: square tower attached to keeper's dwelling
steel skeletal tower with automatic beacon

access.note: Private residence. Grounds and dwelling closed to the public (USLHS: not open to public; LighthouseFriends: privately owned, closed).

facts.agency: Private owner (sold 1934 at auction after deactivation)

events.note: Tower and keeper's dwelling built in 1886 on a three-quarter-acre site
Steamer Eolus struck the rocky point at the north end of the island during a storm, before the light was lit
Fog bell signal changed to a double blow every 10 seconds (from every 30); barn built and sea wall repaired
Blower siren with oil engine replaced the fog bell; 833-gallon water tank
Brick engine house built to replace the old fog signal building
Keeper Horace Arnold's notes describe an April 1911 storm as the severest he had seen in 37 years
Lantern and lens removed; light deactivated
Steel skeletal tower with automatic beacon built to the east
Keeper Elmer V. Newton moved to Prudence Island light
Lighthouse and grounds declared surplus and sold at auction
National Register of Historic Places, NRIS 87001698
Federal government sold a vacant lot formerly part of the station at auction for $166,000

corrections.why: USLHS gives the tower as 37 feet from base to lantern centre (about 11.3 m) and the focal height as 45 feet (13.7 m). The 13.0 m figure in the record is from Wikidata and may measure a different point. Not applied; for a human to check.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: USLHS Conanicut roster ends Newton in 1932; LighthouseFriends and the USLHS Prudence Island roster place his move to Prudence Island in 1933, the year the light was deactivated. Both are shown.
The NRHP nomination and LighthouseFriends agree on 1 April 1886; the USLHS record gives 1886.
The NRHP nomination and LighthouseFriends place the change from fog bell to blower siren in 1900; the Light-House Board's 1900 report records the blower siren established for fiscal 1900.

notes_for_editor: (1) The NRHP nomination copy in the cache has only continuation sheets 31-33 and 51-52 (partial OCR; about 6,500 characters); the rest of the nomination was not read. The owner's name in the nomination is deliberately left out; the present owner is a private individual. (2) Keeper names come from the USLHS roster (NARA registers via the Kraig Anderson inventory), matched to the station by position (0.33 km). Each name is also in LighthouseFriends, which is a secondary source; no primary keeper register was read. (3) Printed pages were checked in this pass against the full OCR text of each volume (the archive.org djvu text, read through its running headers): the 1897 fog-bell and barn passage (item 194) falls under the header '58' (the report's index also gives 'Conanicat Island, R. I., 58'); the 1900 blower-siren passage falls under the header '62' (the index gives 'Conanicnt Island, R. I 62'); the 1901 item 206 falls under the header '83', with scan page 121 from corpus.py. Scan images were not viewed. (4) The Eolus wreck is dated only by the paper's 'Saturday evening' in an issue of 6 February 1886; LighthouseFriends places the grounding in the winter of the construction break. The Herald masthead reads 'Narragansett Pier, R.I.'. No 1886 Lighthouse Board report is in the local corpus, so the first lighting rests on the NRHP nomination, LighthouseFriends and the USLHS record. (5) LighthouseFriends is internally inconsistent on the lantern height (45 feet in its data table; 47 feet and 'sixty feet above the bay' in its text) and on the light's colour (it says the lens gave a fixed red light; no other source read gives a characteristic). The characteristic is therefore left out of facts. (6) LighthouseFriends' narrative of Arnold's Conimicut years (the ice floe rescue) concerns Conimicut Light, not this station, and is not used here. (7) Owners of the converted house and the 1934 auction buyers are not named. (8) Record 'light.characteristic' is null; not changed. (9) The NPGallery asset record gives 'Date Published: 2/25/1988'; the story uses that wording, not 'listing date'. (10) The story's 'Two storms' rests on LighthouseFriends' quotation of Arnold's notes; the second storm is undated.
